title: Multiple comparisons
outcome: Explain multiple comparisons using the records and boundaries of this fictional investigation.
scenario: Six declared prompt comparisons. A team performs six valid hypothesis tests and applies a predeclared Bonferroni familywise threshold.
given: Familywise alpha=0.05. Supplied unadjusted p-values are 0.004,0.012,0.02,0.08,0.4,0.9. These values are stipulated, not calculated from invented data.

steps.label: Count the planned tests
steps.detail: There are six tests in the declared family.

steps.label: Apply all six decisions
steps.detail: Only 0.004 is below 0.00833; the other five do not reject under this rule.

explanation: Searching many comparisons provides more chances for false positives. Bonferroni divides the error allowance across the declared family; valid individual p-values are required. A rejected null is not automatically a large or useful improvement.

counterfactual.change: The declared family has ten tests instead of six; keep the listed values unchanged.
counterfactual.prediction: The cutoff becomes 0.005, and only 0.004 among the listed values still rejects.
counterfactual.reason: The error allowance is divided among ten tests; all ten results must be reported, including the four not supplied here.

student_task: Calculate the six-test cutoff and identify which supplied p-values reject. Why must the team count every planned comparison rather than report only its smallest p-value?
teacher_answer: The cutoff is 0.05/6≈0.00833. Only p=0.004 rejects; the other five exceed the cutoff. Reporting just that result conceals the search and its familywise error control.
project_evidence: For the Reproducible AI Research Study, retain an annotated worked trace and the changed-case reasoning. Connect the claim to its records, units and assumptions so another investigator can challenge or reproduce it.
limits: No effect size or real data is supplied. Bonferroni can be conservative and cannot repair invalid p-values or undisclosed outcome-driven test selection.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice distinct from the reserved independent case. No invented significance, real experiment execution or pupil outcome is asserted.
